text.p: The Philadelphia Phillies, who finished the season with the worst record in the National League, fired manager Jim Fregosi on Monday.
Philadelphia, decimated by injuries during the season that ended on Sunday, compiled a mark of 67-95.
No replacement was named but third base coach Larry Bowa is believed to be a leading candidate for the job.
The Phillies were without two of their top players -- outfielder Lenny Dykstra and catcher Darren Daulton -- for most of the 1996 season.
Dykstra, who had back surgery in July, played in only 40 games. Daulton, again bothered by knee problems, played in just five.
Starting pitchers Curt Schilling, Sid Fernandez and Mike Grace also spent time on the disabled list with assorted injuries.
The 54-year-old Fregosi managed the last six seasons at Philadelphia.

He guided the Phils to victory over the Atlanta Braves in the 1993 National League Championship Series and a trip to the World Series, where the Phillies fell to Toronto. Since then the Phillies laboured through three consecutive losing seasons.
Fregosi replaced Nick Leyva as manager in 1991 and compiled a 431-463 record in six seasons with the team.
Fregosi, who previously managed the California Angels and Chicago White Sox of the American League, has a career record of 861-938.
